## Pre-Typhoon vs Post-Typhoon Air Quality Analysis (2025-07-19 to 2025-07-21)

### Network-Wide Metrics

| Metric | Pre-Typhoon (Jul 19) | Post-Typhoon (Jul 21) | Change |
|--------|---------------------|----------------------|--------|
| **PM2.5 (µg/m³)** | 19.01 | 7.31 | −11.70 (−61.6%) |
| **AQHI** | 3.35 | 2.76 | −0.59 (−17.7%) |

### Pollution Clearance Effectiveness

The tropical cyclone system demonstrated **strong pollution clearance capability**, reducing network-wide mean PM2.5 by **11.70 µg/m³** (a 61.6% reduction). The middle day (July 20) recorded an even lower PM2.5 of 4.69 µg/m³, indicating the storm passage itself provided the most aggressive washout, with a slight rebound on July 21 as urban activities resumed. AQHI remained in the **LOW** risk category (1–3) throughout all three days, dropping from 3.35 pre-typhoon to 2.76 post-typhoon.

### Optimal Timing for Outdoor Activities Post-Storm

On July 21 (post-typhoon), the cleanest hours for outdoor activities were in the **early morning (02:00–07:00)**, with PM2.5 concentrations between **4.3–6.1 µg/m³** and AQHI around 2.7–2.9. The six best hours ranked by lowest PM2.5 are:

1. **02:00** — PM2.5: 4.31 µg/m³, AQHI: 2.83
2. **05:00** — PM2.5: 4.38 µg/m³, AQHI: 2.89
3. **04:00** — PM2.5: 4.64 µg/m³, AQHI: 2.72
4. **03:00** — PM2.5: 5.09 µg/m³, AQHI: 2.83
5. **06:00** — PM2.5: 5.20 µg/m³, AQHI: 2.89
6. **07:00** — PM2.5: 6.10 µg/m³, AQHI: 2.89

Pollution levels begin rising after 08:00, peaking around 13:00 (PM2.5: 11.1 µg/m³), then gradually decline through the evening. For practical outdoor activity planning, **early morning (before 08:00) and late evening (after 19:00)** offer the best air quality on the first day following storm passage.
